subject: maths
question: In ΔDEF, M and N are the points on sides DE and DF respectively. MN is parallel to EF and MN ∶ EF = 2 ∶ 5. If DE = 60 cm, then what is the length of ME?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **MN || EF**, by the properties of **similar triangles** (ΔDMN ∼ ΔDEF), the ratio of the corresponding sides is equal to the ratio of **MN** and **EF**.

Ratio **DM : DE = MN : EF = 2 : 5**

Given **DE** = 5 units = **60 cm** ⇒ 1 unit = **12 cm**

**DM** = 2 units = 2 × 12 = **24 cm**

**ME = DE − DM** = 60 − 24 = **36 cm**

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **DE** = 60 cm, **MN || EF**, and **MN : EF** = 2 : 5.

**Formula Used:** According to the **Basic Proportionality Theorem** or **Thales Theorem**, if a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio. For similar triangles **ΔDMN** and **ΔDEF**, **DM/DE = MN/EF**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ffda10d9228b07f6430a0c3412587b80127d112956ec21759939c41859fee2b6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In **ΔDMN** and **ΔDEF**, **∠D** is common and **∠DMN = ∠DEF** (corresponding angles as **MN || EF**).

⇒ **ΔDMN ∼ ΔDEF** (By **AA similarity** criterion).

⇒ **DM/DE = MN/EF**

⇒ **DM/60 = 2/5**

⇒ **DM = (2 × 60) / 5**

⇒ **DM = 24 cm**

⇒ Now, **ME = DE − DM**

⇒ **ME = 60 − 24 = 36 cm**

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem)

If a line is parallel to one side of a triangle, it divides the other two sides in the same ratio. Formula: **DM/ME = DN/NF**.

Similarity Ratios

For similar triangles, the ratio of all corresponding linear components (sides, medians, altitudes, perimeters) is equal. **Side Ratio = Perimeter Ratio**.

Area Ratio Property

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides. **Area(ΔDMN) / Area(ΔDEF) = (MN/EF)²**.</p
